scope: Exodus 7–8, all 57 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public 7:1–25 = Hebrew 7:1–25; public 8:1–4 = Hebrew 7:26–29; public 8:5–32 = Hebrew 8:1–28.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Preserves the God/prophet relationship, with like making its relational force clear and a note retaining the more direct Hebrew formulation.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “See, I have made you God to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother will be your prophet.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Look, I have made you like God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “See, I have made you God to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother will be your prophet.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes Moses’ receiving and speaking from Aaron’s speech to Pharaoh while retaining the goal of release.
verses.before: You are to speak all that I command you, and Aaron your brother is to speak to Pharaoh, so that he will send the Israelites out of his land.
verses.after: You must speak everything I command you. Your brother Aaron must speak to Pharaoh so that he will let the Israelites leave his land.
verses.tsw_comparator: You are to speak all that I command you, and Aaron your brother is to speak to Pharaoh, so that he will send the Israelites out of his land.

verses.rationale: Keeps God explicitly as the agent of hardening and retains both signs and wonders, without adding a theory explaining the action.
verses.before: Yet I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and I will multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.
verses.after: But I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and I will multiply my signs and wonders in Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and I will multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Preserves the plural audience, divine hand, organized companies, and their identification as the people rather than separate armies.
verses.before: Pharaoh will not listen to you. Then I will lay my hand on Egypt and bring out my companies, my people, the Israelites, from the land of Egypt by great acts of judgment.
verses.after: Pharaoh will not listen to you. Then I will lay my hand on Egypt and bring my companies—my people, the Israelites—out of Egypt with great acts of judgment.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh will not listen to you. Then I will lay my hand on Egypt and bring out my companies, my people, the Israelites, from the land of Egypt by great acts of judgment.

verses.rationale: Retains knowing as the stated outcome and the repeated divine hand and bringing-out language.
verses.before: The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I stretch out my hand against Egypt and bring the Israelites out from among them.”
verses.after: The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I stretch out my hand over Egypt and bring the Israelites out from among them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I stretch out my hand against Egypt and bring the Israelites out from among them.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the doubled report of compliance instead of compressing a meaningful recurring formula.
verses.before: Moses and Aaron did as the LORD commanded them; so they did.
verses.after: Moses and Aaron did so. They did just what the LORD had commanded them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses and Aaron did as the LORD commanded them; so they did.

verses.rationale: Preserves both ages and their relation to the time of speaking without importing a chronological scheme.
verses.before: Moses was eighty years old and Aaron eighty-three years old when they spoke to Pharaoh.
verses.after: Moses was eighty years old and Aaron eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses was eighty years old and Aaron eighty-three years old when they spoke to Pharaoh.

verses.rationale: Keeps both recipients and lets the sentence continue naturally into the instruction at the next label.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,

verses.rationale: Renders the demand’s for-yourselves force and distinguishes tannin as serpent from chapter 4’s snake, without fixing a zoological species.
verses.before: “When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, ‘Perform a wonder for yourselves,’ then you are to say to Aaron, ‘Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh. Let it become a great serpent.’”
verses.after: “When Pharaoh says to you, ‘Show a wonder to prove yourselves,’ tell Aaron, ‘Take your staff and throw it down in front of Pharaoh.’ It will become a serpent.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, ‘Perform a wonder for yourselves,’ then you are to say to Aaron, ‘Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh. Let it become a great serpent.’”

verses.rationale: Retains both men’s obedience and Aaron as the specifically named performer with his own staff.
verses.before: Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh, and they did as the LORD commanded. Aaron threw down his staff before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a great serpent.
verses.after: Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did just as the LORD had commanded. Aaron threw his staff down before Pharaoh and his servants, and it became a serpent.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh, and they did as the LORD commanded. Aaron threw down his staff before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a great serpent.

verses.rationale: Keeps the named kinds of court specialists and the narrator’s report of their action without explaining it as illusion or demonic power.
verses.before: Then Pharaoh also called for the wise men and the sorcerers, and they too—the magicians of Egypt—did the same by their secret arts.
verses.after: Pharaoh also summoned the wise men and sorcerers. These Egyptian magicians did the same thing through their secret arts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Pharaoh also called for the wise men and the sorcerers, and they too—the magicians of Egypt—did the same by their secret arts.

verses.rationale: Preserves the source’s return to staff language during the swallowing rather than harmonizing it to snakes throughout.
verses.before: Each threw down his staff, and they became great serpents. But Aaron’s staff swallowed up their staffs.
verses.after: Each man threw down his staff, and the staffs became serpents. But Aaron’s staff swallowed their staffs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Each threw down his staff, and they became great serpents. But Aaron’s staff swallowed up their staffs.

verses.rationale: Follows the intransitive description of the heart without inserting God or Pharaoh as a stated causing agent in this verse.
verses.before: Yet Pharaoh’s heart became firm, and he did not listen to them, as the LORD had spoken.
verses.after: Yet Pharaoh’s heart grew hard, and he did not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet Pharaoh’s heart became firm, and he did not listen to them, as the LORD had spoken.

verses.rationale: Renders the heavy-heart idiom as unyielding, with its literal image in a note and the explicit refusal retained.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh’s heart is heavy; he refuses to send the people away.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh’s heart is unyielding. He refuses to let the people go.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh’s heart is heavy; he refuses to send the people away.

verses.rationale: Retains the morning appointment, riverbank, staff, and different Hebrew snake term without inventing Pharaoh’s reason for going to the water.
verses.before: Go to Pharaoh in the morning. Look, he is going out to the water. Stand to meet him on the bank of the Nile, and take in your hand the staff that was changed into a snake.
verses.after: Go to Pharaoh in the morning as he goes out to the water. Stand at the bank of the Nile to meet him, and take in your hand the staff that turned into a snake.
verses.tsw_comparator: Go to Pharaoh in the morning. Look, he is going out to the water. Stand to meet him on the bank of the Nile, and take in your hand the staff that was changed into a snake.

verses.rationale: Makes the nested message clear while retaining its familiar demand and the continuing failure to listen.
verses.before: Say to him, ‘The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, sent me to you, saying, “Send my people away, that they may serve me in the wilderness.” But look, until now you have not listened.
verses.after: Tell him, ‘The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, sent me to you with this message: “Let my people go so they may serve me in the wilderness.” But until now you have not listened.
verses.tsw_comparator: Say to him, ‘The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, sent me to you, saying, “Send my people away, that they may serve me in the wilderness.” But look, until now you have not listened.

verses.rationale: Keeps the first-person divine declaration and in-my-hand wording without changing blood into an inferred natural discoloration.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: By this you will know that I am the LORD. Look, with the staff that is in my hand I am striking the water in the Nile, and it will be changed into blood.
verses.after: This is what the LORD says: “By this you will know that I am the LORD. I am about to strike the Nile’s water with the staff in my hand, and it will turn to blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: By this you will know that I am the LORD. Look, with the staff that is in my hand I am striking the water in the Nile, and it will be changed into blood.

verses.rationale: Preserves fish deaths, stench, and the wearying difficulty of drinking, distinct from the explicit inability stated in the fulfillment.
verses.before: The fish in the Nile will die, the Nile will stink, and the Egyptians will be unable to drink water from the Nile.’”
verses.after: The fish in the Nile will die, the river will stink, and the Egyptians will struggle to drink its water.”’”
verses.tsw_comparator: The fish in the Nile will die, the Nile will stink, and the Egyptians will be unable to drink water from the Nile.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves Aaron’s instruction, all four water descriptions, and the wood/stone phrase, with containers identified as an interpretive supply in a note.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt—over their rivers, their canals, their pools, and every collection of their waters—and they will become blood. There will be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, even in the wood and in the stone.’”
verses.after: The LORD told Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Take your staff and stretch out your hand over Egypt’s waters—its rivers, canals, ponds, and every gathering of water—so they become blood.’ There will be blood throughout Egypt, even in containers of wood and stone.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt—over their rivers, their canals, their pools, and every collection of their waters—and they will become blood. There will be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, even in the wood and in the stone.’”

verses.rationale: Leaves the singular performer unnamed as in the Hebrew, with the likely Aaron referent noted; keeps the witnesses and all-water statement.
verses.before: Moses and Aaron did so, as the LORD commanded. He raised the staff and struck the water in the Nile before the eyes of Pharaoh and before the eyes of his servants, and all the water in the Nile was changed into blood.
verses.after: Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD commanded. He raised the staff and struck the Nile’s water before the eyes of Pharaoh and his servants. All the water in the Nile turned to blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses and Aaron did so, as the LORD commanded. He raised the staff and struck the water in the Nile before the eyes of Pharaoh and before the eyes of his servants, and all the water in the Nile was changed into blood.

verses.rationale: Retains the ecological harm and explicit inability to drink as the narrative’s fulfillment without proposing an external mechanism.
verses.before: The fish in the Nile died, and the Nile stank. The Egyptians could not drink water from the Nile, and there was blood throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.after: The fish in the Nile died, and the river stank. The Egyptians could not drink its water. There was blood throughout Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fish in the Nile died, and the Nile stank. The Egyptians could not drink water from the Nile, and there was blood throughout all the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keeps the magicians’ reported action and continued state of the heart, clarifying the hearers without inventing a supply of unaffected water.
verses.before: But the magicians of Egypt did the same by their secret arts. Pharaoh’s heart became firm, and he did not listen to them, as the LORD had spoken.
verses.after: The Egyptian magicians did the same through their secret arts. Pharaoh’s heart remained hard, and he did not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the magicians of Egypt did the same by their secret arts. Pharaoh’s heart became firm, and he did not listen to them, as the LORD had spoken.

verses.rationale: Retains both his departure and the heart idiom linking his inattention with the hardening descriptions.
verses.before: Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he did not set his heart even on this.
verses.after: Pharaoh turned and went into his house. He did not take even this to heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he did not set his heart even on this.

verses.rationale: Keeps the collective search and its stated cause without claiming that they successfully found safe water.
verses.before: All the Egyptians dug around the Nile for water to drink, because they could not drink from the water of the Nile.
verses.after: All the Egyptians dug around the Nile for drinking water because they could not drink from the river.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the Egyptians dug around the Nile for water to drink, because they could not drink from the water of the Nile.

verses.rationale: Preserves the precise elapsed interval and the LORD as the stated agent of striking in the closing notice.
verses.before: Seven days were completed after the LORD struck the Nile.
verses.after: Seven full days passed after the LORD struck the Nile.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seven days were completed after the LORD struck the Nile.

verses.rationale: Binds public 8:1 to Hebrew 7:26 and preserves the renewed message with its serving purpose; nested speech continues through verse 4.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh and say to him, ‘Thus says the LORD: Send my people away, that they may serve me.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and tell him, ‘This is what the LORD says: “Let my people go so they may serve me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh and say to him, ‘Thus says the LORD: Send my people away, that they may serve me.

verses.rationale: Binds to Hebrew 7:27 and retains the conditional refusal and complete territorial scope without adding a natural mechanism.
verses.before: But if you refuse to send them away, look, I am striking all your territory with frogs.
verses.after: If you refuse to let them go, I am about to strike your whole territory with frogs.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you refuse to send them away, look, I am striking all your territory with frogs.

verses.rationale: Binds to Hebrew 7:28 and retains every location, from royal bed to food preparation, and the repeated into movement.
verses.before: The Nile will swarm with frogs, and they will come up and enter your house, your bedroom, and upon your bed; into the houses of your servants and among your people; into your ovens and your kneading bowls.
verses.after: The Nile will teem with frogs. They will come up into your house, into your bedroom, onto your bed, into your servants’ houses and among your people, into your ovens and your kneading bowls.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Nile will swarm with frogs, and they will come up and enter your house, your bedroom, and upon your bed; into the houses of your servants and among your people; into your ovens and your kneading bowls.

verses.rationale: Binds to Hebrew 7:29 and preserves the bodily invasion as well as all three affected groups.
verses.before: The frogs will come up upon you, upon your people, and upon all your servants.’”
verses.after: The frogs will climb onto you, your people, and all your servants.”’”
verses.tsw_comparator: The frogs will come up upon you, upon your people, and upon all your servants.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps Moses as recipient and Aaron as instructed actor with all three water settings; source binding records the four-verse numbering offset.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers, over the canals, and over the pools, and bring up the frogs over the land of Egypt.’”
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers, canals, and ponds, and bring frogs up over Egypt.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers, over the canals, and over the pools, and bring up the frogs over the land of Egypt.’”

verses.rationale: Retains Aaron’s completed gesture and the collective frog term as a multitude covering Egypt.
verses.before: So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frog came up and covered the land of Egypt.
verses.after: Aaron stretched out his hand over Egypt’s waters. Frogs came up and covered the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frog came up and covered the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Preserves the magicians’ multiplication of the affliction rather than treating their action as its removal.
verses.before: But the magicians did the same by their secret arts, and they brought up frogs over the land of Egypt.
verses.after: The magicians did the same through their secret arts; they too brought frogs up over Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the magicians did the same by their secret arts, and they brought up frogs over the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retains the request to both men, Pharaoh’s affected people, and his promise of release for sacrifice.
verses.before: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, “Pray earnestly to the LORD, that he may remove the frogs from me and from my people; then I will send the people away, that they may sacrifice to the LORD.”
verses.after: Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron. “Plead with the LORD to remove the frogs from me and my people,” he said. “Then I will let the people go to sacrifice to the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, “Pray earnestly to the LORD, that he may remove the frogs from me and from my people; then I will send the people away, that they may sacrifice to the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Renders the unusual honor-over-me idiom as granting the timing choice while keeping all beneficiaries and the Nile exception.
verses.before: Moses said to Pharaoh, “Take the honor over me: When will I pray for you, for your servants, and for your people, to cut off the frogs from you and from your houses? Only in the Nile will they remain.”
verses.after: Moses said to Pharaoh, “The honor is yours: tell me when to plead for you, your servants, and your people, to rid you and your houses of the frogs. They will remain only in the Nile.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to Pharaoh, “Take the honor over me: When shall I pray for you, for your servants, and for your people, to cut off the frogs from you and from your houses? Only in the Nile shall they remain.”

verses.rationale: Clarifies the two speakers, retains Pharaoh’s chosen date, and keeps knowing as the announced purpose.
verses.before: He said, “Tomorrow.” And he said, “According to your word, so that you may know that there is none like the LORD our God.
verses.after: “Tomorrow,” Pharaoh answered. Moses said, “It will be as you say, so you may know that there is no one like the LORD our God.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Tomorrow.” And he said, “According to your word, so that you may know that there is none like the LORD our God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated full removal list and the repeated exception instead of shortening the assurance.
verses.before: “The frogs will depart from you, from your houses, from your servants, and from your people. Only in the Nile will they remain.”
verses.after: The frogs will leave you, your houses, your servants, and your people. They will remain only in the Nile.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “The frogs shall depart from you, from your houses, from your servants, and from your people. Only in the Nile shall they remain.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Moses as the one crying out; uses a passive for the relative clause whose Hebrew subject is not named rather than deciding silently between divine and mediated agency.
verses.before: Then Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried out to the LORD concerning the frogs that he had brought upon Pharaoh.
verses.after: Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh. Moses cried out to the LORD about the frogs that had been brought upon Pharaoh.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried out to the LORD concerning the frogs that he had brought upon Pharaoh.

verses.rationale: Retains the response to Moses and three places of death, using courtyards for the contextually possible settlements/courts term.
verses.before: And the LORD did according to the word of Moses. The frogs died in the houses, in the courtyards, and in the fields.
verses.after: The LORD did as Moses asked. The frogs died in the houses, courtyards, and fields.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD did according to the word of Moses. The frogs died in the houses, in the courtyards, and in the fields.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated heaps image and the land’s stench, connecting the sensory harm with the preceding water plague.
verses.before: They piled them up, heap upon heap, and the land stank.
verses.after: They piled them up in heaps upon heaps, and the land stank.
verses.tsw_comparator: They piled them up, heap upon heap, and the land stank.

verses.rationale: Preserves Pharaoh as the explicit hardening agent after relief, unlike the uncaused grammatical descriptions in 7:13 and 7:22.
verses.before: But when Pharaoh saw that there was relief, he hardened his heart and did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken.
verses.after: But when Pharaoh saw that there was relief, he hardened his heart and did not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when Pharaoh saw that there was relief, he hardened his heart and did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken.

verses.rationale: Retains dust as the transformed material and gnats as a conventional but uncertain identification of the insect term.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the land, and it will become gnats throughout all the land of Egypt.’”
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the ground. It will become gnats throughout Egypt.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the land, and it shall become gnats throughout all the land of Egypt.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves collective compliance, Aaron’s specific action, both affected groups, and the full repeated dust-to-gnats claim.
verses.before: And they did so. Aaron stretched out his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the land, and the gnats came upon humans and livestock. All the dust of the land became gnats throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.after: They did so. Aaron stretched out his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the ground. Gnats came upon people and animals; all the dust of the ground became gnats throughout Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they did so. Aaron stretched out his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the land, and the gnats came upon humans and livestock. All the dust of the land became gnats throughout all the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the unsuccessful attempt from earlier successes and keeps animals within the account’s harm.
verses.before: The magicians did the same by their secret arts, trying to bring out the gnats, but they could not. And the gnats were upon humans and livestock.
verses.after: The magicians tried to bring forth gnats through their secret arts, but they could not. The gnats remained on people and animals.
verses.tsw_comparator: The magicians did the same by their secret arts, trying to bring out the gnats, but they could not. And the gnats were upon humans and livestock.

verses.rationale: Retains the finger image and conventional God rendering while noting that the magicians use elohim rather than the divine name; no conversion is inferred.
verses.before: Then the magicians said to Pharaoh, “This is the finger of God.” But Pharaoh’s heart grew strong, and he did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken.
verses.after: The magicians told Pharaoh, “This is the finger of God!” Yet Pharaoh’s heart remained hard, and he did not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the magicians said to Pharaoh, “This is the finger of God.” But Pharaoh’s heart grew strong, and he did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken.

verses.rationale: Preserves the renewed morning confrontation and exact repeated release-and-service demand, with public/source mapping explicit in the ledger.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh. Look, he is going out to the water. Say to him, ‘Thus says the LORD: Send my people away, that they may serve me.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh as he goes out to the water. Tell him, ‘This is what the LORD says: “Let my people go so they may serve me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh. Look, he is going out to the water. Say to him, ‘Thus says the LORD: Send my people away, that they may serve me.

verses.rationale: Retains the send/release word connection and all affected places while noting that flies is an uncertain identification of the swarm term.
verses.before: “For if you do not send my people away, look, I am sending the swarm against you, against your servants, against your people, and into your houses. The houses of the Egyptians will be filled with the swarm, and also the ground on which they are.
verses.after: If you will not let my people go, I will send swarms of flies on you, your servants, your people, and your houses. The Egyptians’ houses will be full of swarms, and so will the ground beneath them.
verses.tsw_comparator: “For if you do not send my people away, look, I am sending the swarm against you, against your servants, against your people, and into your houses. The houses of the Egyptians shall be filled with the swarm, and also the ground on which they are.

verses.rationale: Keeps the specifically stated distinction for Goshen and the spatial claim, with earth as an alternative sense of land noted.
verses.before: “But on that day I will set apart the land of Goshen, where my people dwell, so that no swarm will be there, so that you may know that I, the LORD, am among the land.
verses.after: But on that day I will set apart Goshen, where my people are staying. No swarms will be there, so you may know that I am the LORD in the midst of the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But on that day I will set apart the land of Goshen, where my people dwell, so that no swarm shall be there, in order that you may know that I, the LORD, am in the midst of the land.

verses.rationale: Retains the Masoretic redemption noun through redeeming rather than silently replacing it with a different Hebrew word for distinction; makes the between-people relation readable.
verses.before: “I will set a redemption between my people and your people. Tomorrow this sign will come to pass.’”
verses.after: By redeeming my people, I will set them apart from yours. This sign will happen tomorrow.”’”
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will set a redemption between my people and your people. Tomorrow this sign shall come to pass.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps the LORD’s action, royal and servant households, and the strong land-ruin description without adding a disease diagnosis.
verses.before: And the LORD did so. A heavy swarm came into Pharaoh’s house, into the houses of his servants, and throughout all the land of Egypt. The land was ruined because of the swarm.
verses.after: The LORD did so. Dense swarms came into Pharaoh’s house and his servants’ houses. Throughout Egypt, the land was being ruined by the swarms.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD did so. A heavy swarm came into Pharaoh’s house, into the houses of his servants, and throughout all the land of Egypt. The land was ruined because of the swarm.

verses.rationale: Makes the geographic restriction in Pharaoh’s offer audible without turning it into full release.
verses.before: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, “Go, sacrifice to your God in the land.”
verses.after: Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “Go and sacrifice to your God here in the land.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, “Go, sacrifice to your God in the land.”

verses.rationale: Keeps abomination as a culturally attributed claim and the threatened stoning, with the alternative relation to Egyptian sacred animals noted rather than specified in the text.
verses.before: Yet Moses said, “It would not be right to do so, for we would sacrifice to the LORD our God what is an abomination to the Egyptians. If we sacrifice what is an abomination to the Egyptians before their eyes, will they not stone us?
verses.after: Moses answered, “That would not be right. What we sacrifice to the LORD our God is an abomination to the Egyptians. If we sacrifice what they find abhorrent before their eyes, will they not stone us?
verses.tsw_comparator: But Moses said, “It would not be right to do so, for we would sacrifice to the LORD our God what is an abomination to the Egyptians. If we sacrifice what is an abomination to the Egyptians before their eyes, will they not stone us?

verses.rationale: Retains the journey’s distance and dependence on divine instruction, not a three-day limit on absence.
verses.before: “We will go a journey of three days into the wilderness, and we will sacrifice to the LORD our God, as he tells us.”
verses.after: We must travel three days into the wilderness and sacrifice to the LORD our God as he tells us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “We will go a journey of three days into the wilderness, and we will sacrifice to the LORD our God, as he tells us.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the concession, emphatic distance restriction, and request for intercession as distinct speech acts.
verses.before: Pharaoh said, “I will send you away, so that you may sacrifice to the LORD your God in the wilderness. Only, you must not go too far away. Pray earnestly for me.”
verses.after: Pharaoh said, “I will let you go to sacrifice to the LORD your God in the wilderness. But you must not go far at all. Plead for me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh said, “I will send you away, so that you may sacrifice to the LORD your God in the wilderness. Only, you must not go too far away. Pray earnestly for me.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the timing and Moses’ shift to Pharaoh in the third person, preserving the force of the warning against renewed deception.
verses.before: Moses said, “Look, I am going out from you, and I will pray earnestly to the LORD; and tomorrow the swarm will depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people. Only Pharaoh must not again deal deceitfully by refusing to send the people away to sacrifice to the LORD.”
verses.after: Moses answered, “I am leaving you now, and I will plead with the LORD. Tomorrow the swarms will leave Pharaoh, his servants, and his people. But Pharaoh must not deceive us again by refusing to let the people go to sacrifice to the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said, “Look, I am going out from you, and I will pray earnestly to the LORD; and tomorrow the swarm will depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people. Only Pharaoh must not again deal deceitfully by refusing to send the people away to sacrifice to the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Retains the concise completed departure and prayer rather than expanding it into an unrecorded speech.
verses.before: Then Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed earnestly to the LORD.
verses.after: Moses left Pharaoh and pleaded with the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed earnestly to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the complete three-group removal and the emphatic not-one-remained conclusion.
verses.before: And the LORD did according to the word of Moses, and he removed the swarm from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people. Not one remained.
verses.after: The LORD did as Moses asked. He removed the swarms from Pharaoh, his servants, and his people. Not one remained.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD did according to the word of Moses, and he removed the swarm from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people. Not one remained.

verses.rationale: Retains Pharaoh as the explicit agent and this-time-too repetition, ending the episode with unfulfilled release.
verses.before: Yet Pharaoh hardened his heart this time also, and he did not send the people away.
verses.after: But this time too, Pharaoh hardened his heart and did not let the people go.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Pharaoh hardened his heart this time also, and he did not send the people away.
